## Cloud credentials and API URL
`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval
list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags
at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.
Credential precedence for Cloud commands:
1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still
use it.
3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`
4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)
API URL precedence:
1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their serve
r counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`
Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it
contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries c
redentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error m
asks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own ser
ver: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status`
uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.vali
d` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) an
d successful.
Successful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppress
es it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.
## Cloud project scope
Most Cloud commands pick one project:
1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`

# Local Evals
> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity
> [!NOTE]
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs
with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their exi
sting behavior.
`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model,
grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own
provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.
Results are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run
start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) e
vent, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.
